findings.evidence: 'Start here. For the working method, begin at Ch. 1 (The Token) and follow the canonical workload through Chs. 16–17 and 20–21 (TCO, fleet sizing, fleet optimization and the factory gate, where the numbers pay off), returning to the policy sections later.'
findings.issue: The Preface's 'Start here' reading path skips Chapters 4–15 and 18–19 entirely, yet Chapters 16–17 depend on the Ch 4 canonical scenario and on Ch 7/8 arithmetic the reader would not yet have seen. The recommended path is internally inconsistent with the stated dependency chain ('The chapters build on one another').
findings.fix_instruction: Either revise the 'Start here' path to include Ch 4 and Ch 7–8, or add an explicit caveat that the reader must consult the canonical-scenario box (Ch 4, Table 4-2) before Ch 16.

findings.evidence: 'ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED) … Axis note: [ILLUSTRATIVE] is a provenance tag (Axis 1) only — a non-canonical worked example — and is never a measurement status; measurement status uses ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED or UNMEASURED.'
findings.issue: The ILLUSTRATIVE definition says it is 'paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED', but the very next sentence says '[ILLUSTRATIVE] is a provenance tag (Axis 1) only … and is never a measurement status'. The two sentences are in tension: the first describes ILLUSTRATIVE as a register that pairs with an epistemic status, the second insists it is provenance-only. Readers cannot tell whether ILLUSTRATIVE is Axis 1 or Axis 2.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the ILLUSTRATIVE bullet to state unambiguously: '[ILLUSTRATIVE] is Axis-1 provenance only; it is always paired with an Axis-2 status ([ASSUMPTION] or [DERIVED]) and is never itself an epistemic or measurement status.'

findings.evidence: 'Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED]); Axis 3, measurement status, rides along where a claim's status is known.'
findings.issue: The stated rule is that every load-bearing quantitative claim carries an inline Axis-1/Axis-2 pair. This is violated on the very same page: 'an H100 GPU's 0.989 PFLOPS BF16 dense tensor-core peak and 3.35 TB/s HBM bandwidth' appears in the Preface with no label pair, and hundreds of later values (e.g. p. 22's '140 GB', p. 27's '~1 FLOP/byte') appear bare. The evidence-discipline rule is aspirational, not enforced.
findings.fix_instruction: Either enforce the inline-pair rule throughout (impractical) or downgrade the claim to 'load-bearing claims carry labels inline or via an identified table/section', which is what the book actually does.

findings.evidence: "Evidence boundary — four registers, and where each is used. MEASURED — an instrumented run under the Chapter 14 protocol; used only where the book reports a benchmark it actually ran, never for a planning screen. ANALYTICAL — arithmetic on stated inputs (roofline, KV-residency and capacity screens, the C/W per-host bound and the host counts derived from it): a bound, not an observed rate — not a measured throughput, not a lower guaranteed rate, not SLO-goodput, no p95/p99 guarantee, each conditional on its stated assumptions (e.g. the assumed mean KV residency time). ILLUSTRATIVE — a chosen scenario input or worked example ([canonical scenario] or [ILLUSTRATIVE], paired with ASSUMPTION or DERIVED), on the book's teaching geometry, to be re-derived per deployment; this is a provenance-and-register marker, not a measurement status (see the Axis note below). HYPOTHESIS — reasoned but not yet validated (with UNRESOLVED for questions the book leaves open), used where mechanism is argued without measurement."
findings.issue: Self-contradictory label definitions in the Preface, the document's own rule source. The Preface simultaneously asserts (a) four measurement registers, MEASURED / ANALYTICAL / ILLUSTRATIVE / HYPOTHESIS, each with a stated use; and (b) a three-axis label-pair system in which ILLUSTRATIVE is explicitly reclassified: 'this is a provenance-and-register marker, not a measurement status'. The second clause cancels the fourth register: if ILLUSTRATIVE is a provenance tag and never a measurement status, it cannot simultaneously be one of the four measurement registers. The paragraph then lists ANALYTICAL, SCENARIO-DERIVED, MODELED, MEASURED as the measurement-status vocabulary — five names, of which ANALYTICAL is drawn from the 'four registers' list and three are not in it at all. A reader cannot determine, from the Preface alone, which of the two taxonomies governs a given tag, and the two are used interchangeably throughout the body (e.g. p. 149 '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]' on Fig 7.7 versus p. 169's '[ILLUSTRATIVE][DERIVED]'; and p. 20's 'Forward-looking numbers are marked ILLUSTRATIVE', i.e. ILLUSTRATIVE as a measurement status).
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the Preface 'Evidence boundary' panel so there is exactly one taxonomy: a two-axis label-pair system (Axis 1 provenance ∈ {1P, canonical scenario, ILLUSTRATIVE, 2°, LAB} × Axis 2 epistemic ∈ {FACT, DERIVED, ASSUMPTION, HYPOTHESIS, UNRESOLVED}) plus a separate Axis 3 measurement-status vocabulary (ANALYTICAL / SCENARIO-DERIVED / MODELED / MEASURED / UNMEASURED). Delete the 'four registers' framing, or explicitly subordinate it ('the four registers below are shorthand for the most common (Axis 2, Axis 3) combinations; the label pair is authoritative'). Then sweep the body for any use of ILLUSTRATIVE or HYPOTHESIS as a standalone measurement status and re-tag those rows.

findings.evidence: "A label pair always takes one item from each of the first two axes, e.g. [1P][DERIVED] or [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]; the two tags are set with no space between them and never break across a line." Compare p. 17: "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED])" and "Axis 3, measurement status, rides along where a claim's status is known."
findings.issue: Illegal/undocumented label pair forms in the body that the Preface's rule does not authorise, and no statement of what a three-tag sequence means. The Preface states a label pair takes one item from each of the first two axes, with Axis 3 riding along. The body nonetheless uses multi-tag sequences that combine an Axis-2 epistemic tag with a third tag in a way the Preface never defines, including p. 19 '[1P][DERIVED] (Wan2.2 sampling loop, pinned revision 1ea34ff, retrieved 2026-10-28.)' and p. 135 '[DERIVED] (source keys: each [S#] names one entry in the References chapter...)' — where the bracketed Axis-2 tag is followed by a source key rather than an Axis-3 status. Worse, p. 135 reads: '"[1P][DERIVED] [HYPOTHESIS]"' — no; the actual text is 'These percentages are hypothetical telemetry signatures ... [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]' while the sentence two lines earlier reads 'a decode kernel pinned at ~95% of HBM bandwidth / ~30% of FLOPs [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION]'. The genuine double-pair violation appears at p. 135 in the sentence '[S4][1P][FACT]: the bottleneck-regime difference is the primary motivation for disaggregation' where an Axis-3-style 'MEASURED' claim rides with [1P][FACT], and at p. 139 'DFlash reports over 6× lossless acceleration ... [S5][1P][FACT] — because it reduces weight reads per accepted token' where a paper-reported figure is tagged [1P][FACT] although the Preface reserves [1P] for 'the model vendor's own spec'.
findings.fix_instruction: Either (a) extend the Preface to define the permitted multi-tag sequences (e.g. '[1P][FACT] + MEASURED' and '[S#] [1P][FACT] + SCENARIO-DERIVED') and state that a source key '[S#]' is not an axis tag; or (b) normalise every occurrence so that exactly one Axis-1 tag and one Axis-2 tag appear, with the Axis-3 status either omitted or set in a declared form. Specifically re-check p. 135 ('[S4][1P][FACT]'), p. 138 ('[S5][1P][FACT]'), p. 139 ('[S7][1P][FACT]') and p. 19 ('[1P][FACT] (Wan2.2 sampling loop...)') so the tag set matches the Preface's declared grammar.

findings.issue: Evidence-label taxonomy violation in the Preface's own conventions: ILLUSTRATIVE is used here as a standalone marker on a class of numbers (a measurement/validity status), which the Preface's Axis note on p. 17 explicitly forbids — '"[ILLUSTRATIVE] is a provenance tag (Axis 1) only — a non-canonical worked example — and is never a measurement status'. 'Forward-looking' is a validity/provenance-of-knowledge statement, not a provenance-of-source statement, so the tag cannot express it. There is no tag in the declared vocabulary for 'projected / forward-looking' — [HYPOTHESIS] is the closest but is not used here. This is the same defect family as EV-001 (register taxonomy vs label pairs), in the conventions section rather than the evidence panel.
findings.fix_instruction: Replace with a defined tag, e.g. 'Forward-looking numbers are marked [HYPOTHESIS] (Axis 2) and, where they are worked examples on the canonical geometry, also [canonical scenario][ASSUMPTION]' — and add the forward-looking notion to the Preface's Axis-2 definition so the convention is defined rather than improvised.

findings.evidence: "2. What fits on one host? — weight residency, KV per token, the concurrency floor. (Chs. 3, 7)" ... "5. Who serves it, and how? — batching, parallelism, P/D disaggregation, scheduling. (Chs. 10–11, 20)" ... "Q1 in Part II, Q2–3 in Parts I/III, Q4–5 in Parts III–V, Q6 in Parts IV/VI."
findings.issue: Malformed cross-reference form: the Preface (p. 20) declares the section-reference grammar 'A section reference takes the form § N.M, which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement), not Section 1's fourth subsection.' and adds 'Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3.' The checklist's parentheticals use a bare multi-chapter form '(Chs. 3, 7)' and '(Chs. 10–11, 20)' with no section anchors at all, so the reader cannot tell which of the many sections in Ch 7 or Ch 11 is meant — this is exactly the 'bare §7' family the blind-spot note flags, in a different notation. The 'Q1…Q6' shorthand is also an undocumented reference form: 'Q2–3' is not a section, a chapter or a figure, and no list of 'Q' targets exists anywhere in the book.
findings.fix_instruction: Give each checklist item section-level anchors in the declared § N.M form (e.g. '§ 7.3 and § 7.6', '§ 10.1–§ 11.4, § 20.2'), and either define the Q1–Q6 shorthand explicitly in the Preface (as an index into the six checklist items) or replace it with the same section anchors. Then sweep the book for other bare '(Chs. X, Y)' pointers and add anchors.

findings.evidence: "Cross-references. A section reference takes the form § N.M, which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement), not Section 1's fourth subsection. Where the chapter is named first, the section number may stand alone: Ch. 7 § 3 means Ch. 7, Section 3."
findings.issue: Ambiguous cross-reference rule as written: 'the section number may stand alone' does not specify whether the standalone form is '§ 3' or '§ 7.3', and the example given ('Ch. 7 § 3') uses a bare section number with no chapter digit, which is precisely the malformed '§7' form that the Preface then says it wants to avoid. The rule therefore authorises two incompatible notations and cannot be applied deterministically: '§ 7.3' is Chapter 7 Section 3 under the declared form, but '§ 3' after 'Ch. 7' means the same thing — so the same string '§ 3' means Ch 3 Section 3 in one context and Ch 7 Section 3 in another. The rule needs an explicit disambiguation rule (e.g. 'a standalone section number is always read against the most recently named chapter') plus a statement of what a bare '§ 7' without a chapter context means.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the rule: '§ N.M always means Chapter N, Section M. When a chapter is already named, write § M and read it against that chapter — but never write a bare § N where N could be mistaken for a chapter number: use § N.M in all other contexts.' Then audit the body for the bare '§ N' form and convert to § N.M.

findings.evidence: "In the book's convention (Ch. 2, 4), TTFTe2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill, where tokenization/transfer counts as one combined term." Compare p. 36 (Ch 2): "Written as a sum, end-to-end TTFT is TTFTe2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill."
findings.issue: Preface-vs-Ch.2 formula divergence in the reference form, and an unresolvable pointer. The Preface and Ch. 2 state the identical formula, but the Preface cites it as '(Ch. 2, 4)' — the declared § N.M convention is not used, and more importantly the pointer 'Ch. 2, 4' is ambiguous: does it mean Ch. 2 and Ch. 4 (both chapters), or Ch. 2 Section 4? Under the Preface's own rule that '§ 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4', the string 'Ch. 2, 4' has no defined interpretation. The same pattern recurs at p. 36: 'Ch 4 §4.3 quotes this formula verbatim' (a mixed 'Ch N §M.M' form that the Preface's 'write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3' rule permits only in the first variant, but here the decimal is doubled in a way that collides with the § N.M grammar), and at p. 20: 'The book’s convention (Ch. 2, 4)'.
findings.fix_instruction: Normalise every instance: use '§ 2.1 and § 4.3' rather than '(Ch. 2, 4)', and replace 'Ch 4 §4.3' with '§ 4.3'. Sweep the full document for the 'Ch N §N.M' doubled-decimal form and for comma-separated chapter lists without section anchors.

findings.chapter: Preface — How the book is organized
findings.evidence: List of Figures begins (p. 9) with '1 The architect's decision loop — the book's spine . . . ix' and '2 Reading the book two ways . . . x' — i.e. the two Preface figures are numbered 1 and 2 — and the List of Figures continues '1.1 The KV cache … 9', '1.2 How a token travels … 10', '2.1 The canonical end-to-end inference pipeline … 20'.
findings.issue: Figure-numbering namespace collision: the Preface figures are numbered '1' and '2' in the same List of Figures that then numbers Ch. 1's figures '1.1' and '1.2' and Ch. 2's '2.1'. A reader following the declared appendix convention (p. 20: 'the appendix's figures carry A.N') and the chapter convention (Fig N.M) has no rule for the front-matter figures: 'Fig 1' (Preface decision loop) and 'Fig 1.1' (KV cache) and 'Ch. 1 Fig 1' all become plausible readings of the same string, and the body refers to figures only as 'Fig 2.1', 'Fig 7.7', 'Fig A.2'. The book's own cross-reference grammar (p. 20) declares '§ N.M' for sections but never declares a figure-reference grammar, so the collision is unresolvable from the rules.
findings.fix_instruction: Renumber the two Preface figures to 'P.1' and 'P.2' (and update the List of Figures and any body references), or declare an explicit figure-reference grammar in the Preface — e.g. 'Fig N.M refers to Chapter N; Preface figures are Fig F1–F2; appendix figures are Fig A.N' — so that no string is ambiguous.

findings.evidence: "Every load-bearing quantitative claim carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair (e.g. [1P][DERIVED]); Axis 3, measurement status, rides along where a claim’s status is known. A claim carries the labels directly (inline) or via an identified table or section that states them (e.g. a worked-example table whose header or footnote gives provenance and status for every row); purely illustrative or rhetorical numbers that no later calculation depends on may carry them in the surrounding prose — exceptions are defined unambiguously in the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter."
findings.issue: Two-claims-in-one-rule defect with an internal contradiction. The rule says every load-bearing quantitative claim carries the pair inline, then immediately allows 'via an identified table or section that states them', then allows 'purely illustrative or rhetorical numbers' to carry labels only in surrounding prose — and defers the exception definitions to a chapter the reader has not yet reached. The contradiction is that a claim 'via an identified table' cannot carry an inline pair, yet the same paragraph asserts that every load-bearing claim 'carries Axes 1 and 2 as an inline pair'. This is the rule that the body then implements inconsistently (e.g. p. 90 Table 4-2 carries per-row Axis-1/Axis-2 tags — compliant — but p. 102's cost-basis table and p. 116's Table 5-2 mix tagged and untagged rows, and p. 131's Fig 6.2 note leaves the synthetic stream's construction untagged in the caption). The rule's own escape clause ('exceptions are defined unambiguously in the Sources, Method, and Reproducibility chapter') means the operative definition of the label system is not in the Preface where the system is introduced.
findings.fix_instruction: Rewrite the rule as three explicit, non-overlapping sentences: (1) every load-bearing quantity carries an Axis-1 and Axis-2 tag, inline or in the caption/footnote of the identified table or figure that contains it; (2) the Axis-3 status is optional but must appear when the status is known; (3) rhetorical numbers that no calculation depends on may be untagged. Move the exception definitions into the Preface itself and delete the deferral to the later chapter, or state that the later chapter's definitions override the Preface's.

findings.evidence: "Every architectural decision has a measurable trade-off." (repeated from page 1)
findings.issue: The text 'Every architectural decision has a measurable trade-off' appears on the Title Page and again on the copyright page (or similar front matter). While not an error, ensure it is intentional branding and not a duplication error from a layout tool.
findings.fix_instruction: Confirm intent of repeated tagline in front matter.
